parsed.explanation: The combined regime is national law operating locally: same-sex conduct lawful since 1815, marriage equality (2013), goods/services discrimination bans (2001), gender-identity discrimination ban (2012), and a 2004 hate-speech offence all apply at the island, with active community infrastructure (2025 events) and functioning courts and administration. No trans-specific entry, document, street-violence or enforcement exposure is documented for the island; in a well-documented state that silence is mildly favourable. The one heavy negative is custody: placement follows the identity document's marker, most trans detainees end up in all-male facilities where they are threatened, and the national watchdog's 2021 finding of persisting 'serious violations' recurs unremedied. That is severe but conditional on detention, which is improbable for a visitor here.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No record of trans-specific border, document-mismatch or secondary-screening friction; national document rules apply with no island-specific procedure.
entry_documents.protection: National anti-discrimination law (goods/services 2001; gender identity 2012) and the 2004 hate-speech offence operate locally through the department's own services.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry and identity checks are national functions administered in the department; a document discrepancy would be handled under mainland rules with ordinary judicial recourse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented. Criminal-procedure placement follows the gender marker on identity documents; most trans detainees are held in all-male facilities where other detainees threaten them. Watchdog (25 May 2021) finds 'persistence of serious violations' of transgender detainees' fundamental rights across all national places of deprivation of liberty, from referrals since 2010 (~40 persons).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National detention watchdog inspections and referrals exist; anti-discrimination and hate-crime provisions apply in principle.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: The department's establishments are the governing state's prisons, so mainland placement rules and watchdog findings bind them; the watchdog's on-site interviews were conducted elsewhere, a coverage limitation rather than a local difference.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No island-specific layer; the exposure is the national placement regime itself, applied without local mitigation or variation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitution applies the full national framework, including marriage equality and anti-discrimination law, to the department with no derogation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: One system only: national rules, departmental courts, registry offices and prisons; no subnational variation is recorded, so local practice tracks the social setting of an encounter, not a distinct rule.

care_services.protection: Gender-identity discrimination has been prohibited in goods and services nationally since 2012, which would cover service settings a visitor enters.
care_services.interaction: Gender-recognition procedure, gender-affirming care and youth transition are national matters under the framework in force locally, not sourced as island findings.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented in custody only: trans detainees are placed by document marker into all-male facilities where they are threatened, and the watchdog records persisting serious rights violations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Homophobic, sexist, racist and xenophobic public comments have been criminalised since 31 December 2004 (fine and/or imprisonment); gender-identity discrimination prohibited since 2012; same-sex conduct lawful since 1815; marriage equality since 2013.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and official framing are protective outside custody, while the custodial institutions themselves enforce a hostile placement rule efficiently — liability, not recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No record of how a travelling family or minor would be treated, or of youth-specific measures.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage equality, anti-discrimination and hate-speech provisions apply uniformly to a travelling family under the national framework.
minors_guardians.interaction: Any guardianship, custody or youth-care question would be governed by national law administered in the department; no island-specific variant exists.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No island-specific figures on anti-trans violence or island enforcement record were located; national hate-crime statistics exist only at governing-state level.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2004 hate-speech offence and 2012 gender-identity discrimination ban; a functioning rule-of-law state whose record generally leaves traces of incidents and enforcement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of island data in an otherwise well-documented national record is mildly favourable, but it is not proof of safety for the island specifically.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Watchdog findings recur across years without documented remediation, corroborating an unremedied custody exposure; no island-specific enforcement record exists.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Departmental courts, administrative services and registry offices process discrimination and hate-crime claims under national law; fines and imprisonment attach to hate speech; marriage and equality regime fully available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor's complaint would run through the same national apparatus residents use; oversight exists but has not corrected the placement practice it documents.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher. Anchor 0.55-B has routine extended secondary screening, frequent refused admission under discretionary public-order grounds and slow, rarely revised remedies. This dossier documents no trans-specific entry friction, refusal practice or administrative limbo, and instead records statutory anti-discrimination and hate-speech protection with functioning courts.

Roughly comparable, differently composed. Anchor 0.75-C pairs trained, respectful border staff with brief humiliating detention and wide officer discretion but low severity. This dossier is stronger on statutory protection and community infrastructure yet worse in custody, where document-marker placement into all-male facilities with threats and persisting watchdog violations is documented.

Lower. Anchor 0.85-A's equality law produces apologies, discipline and compensation after refusals, with only isolated friction. Here the corresponding institutions document a hostile placement rule they enforce and a watchdog repeatedly recording unremedied serious violations against transgender detainees — a tier-1 state-imposed exposure absent from the 0.85 profile.

parsed.synthesis: National law governs the island without local variation, giving the visitor the mainland package: long-standing decriminalisation, marriage equality, goods/services and gender-identity discrimination bans, a hate-speech offence, and an active LGBT network with current events. Everyday exposure — border, hotels, streets — has no documented trans-specific restriction, and in a well-documented state that silence plus the protective statutes is meaningful. The counterweight is custody: placement follows the passport's marker, most trans detainees end up in male facilities where they are threatened, and the watchdog's serious-violations finding recurs without remedy, so efficient institutions are here enforcing a hostile rule. Because detention is improbable for an ordinary visitor, this severe but conditional exposure holds the score below the 0.85 acceptance-with-working-remedies tier rather than into reduced protection bands.
